messages:
Noura El-Khoury: Heads up: partner team at Northshore Cloud (marketplace + integrations) wants to co-market the latency/$ benchmark report. They’re asking for (1) approved blurb, (2) co-branded 1-pager/slide, and (3) timing for marketplace listing update. Can we align on what we’ll offer + approval flow?

Ben Carter: Yep. What’s their target timeline? We’re trying to keep launch week tight.

Noura El-Khoury: They asked if they can post same day as our launch + update their marketplace listing within 24h. Also want to link directly to the PDF + landing page.

Camila Reyes: We can do same-day, but ONLY if they stick to approved language + use our landing page as primary CTA (not a rehost). We need to avoid “#1 fastest” vibes.

Soojin Lee: +1. For partners, I’d prefer a short “how to talk about it” section: what latency/$ means, what we measured, what we didn’t.

Tyler Benson: From attribution side: if they’re posting, we need UTMs consistent across channels. I can generate a partner UTM template and share w/ Noura.

Ben Carter: Great. Also: are we okay with marketplace listing update before embargo lifts? If they push live early, it’ll leak.

Noura El-Khoury: They said they can follow embargo if we give them the date/time. But their marketplace review process can take 2–5 business days, so they want to submit assets early.

Talia Benson: That’s consistent w/ other partners. We can provide “embargoed for review” assets with an explicit “DO NOT PUBLISH BEFORE <date/time>” header. Need Legal/Comms alignment though.

Michael Grant: Legal perspective: review submission pre-embargo is fine as long as (a) partner agrees in writing to embargo, (b) assets are marked confidential/embargoed, (c) they don’t add their own claims beyond what we provide. If they edit copy, we need to re-approve.

Camila Reyes: Can we make this simple:
- We provide a fixed co-marketing kit (approved blurbs + 1 slide + logo lockup rules + links)
- Partners can only use verbatim copy
- Any modifications route back to us for approval

Elliot Price: For web/docs links: landing page will be on redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar (final path TBD). PDF will be behind that page. Please do NOT let them deep-link to a temporary Drive URL.

Ben Carter: Do we have the partner kit doc already? I remember a Drive file.

Noura El-Khoury: Draft exists: Google Drive → shared_drives/go-to-market/partner-co-marketing-kit (still has placeholders). I can clean + finalize today if we agree on what’s included.

Soojin Lee: Include:
1) 2–3 approved blurbs (short/medium)
2) “Do/Don’t” list (no absolute superiority, include region/workload caveat)
3) Approved headline options (e.g., “production economics benchmark” vs “latency/$ report”)
4) Link policy (landing page primary)

Tyler Benson: And a UTM block:
- source=partner
- medium=marketplace or co-marketing
- campaign=benchmark-latency-per-dollar
- content=<partnername>-<asset>
I’ll DM Noura a few exact examples once we pick naming.

Ben Carter: Marketplace timing question: what do we want them to update? Just a “Benchmarks” section and link?

Noura El-Khoury: They suggested:
- marketplace listing: add “Benchmarked latency/$ across NA/EU/APAC regions” bullet + link to report
- a short announcement post in their partner portal
- optional co-branded slide for their field teams

Camila Reyes: For marketplace listing, keep it factual:
- “See Redwood’s published benchmark methodology and results”
- “Results vary by region/model/workload”
No “best”/“leading” adjectives.

Michael Grant: Agree. Also avoid implying endorsement by Northshore Cloud. Wording like “Available on Northshore Cloud Marketplace” is fine; “Northshore Cloud validated Redwood’s results” is not.

Talia Benson: Process proposal:
1) Noura compiles kit v1 today
2) Soojin reviews messaging + “Do/Don’t”
3) Michael does legal pass (claims + logo usage language)
4) Camila final approval
5) Send to partner w/ embargo note + instruction: “no edits without written re-approval”

Ben Carter: Works. Deadline wise: I’d like kit locked by EOD tomorrow so partner can submit to marketplace review.

Elliot Price: One more: if they want screenshots/charts, we should provide specific exports (don’t want them screenshotting drafts). Are we allowing charts in partner materials?

Camila Reyes: Limited. Provide 1–2 approved charts max, already labeled with our disclaimers. Otherwise they’ll crop out caveats.

Soojin Lee: +1. If we do charts, bake in caption text: “Measured on Redwood Inference platform under published methodology; see appendix for details.”

Noura El-Khoury: Got it. I’ll include:
- 2 blurbs
- 1 co-branded slide (w/ chart placeholder or approved chart)
- 1 “marketplace listing copy” block (verbatim)
- UTM guidance
- Embargo banner

Tyler Benson: Re UTMs: for marketplace listing vs partner blog post, please keep separate `medium` so we can attribute. E.g. marketplace vs partner_blog.

Ben Carter: Who’s handling partner approvals / signatures? Do we need a formal embargo doc?

Michael Grant: Email acceptance is okay for embargo if it’s explicit: “We agree not to publish before <timestamp> and will use provided assets verbatim.” No need for a separate NDA if we’re not sharing anything beyond marketing assets.

Talia Benson: I’ll draft the boilerplate email language and share in-thread.

Elliot Price: Please also tell them: no mirroring PDF. We’ve had stale PDF issues before. Link to landing page only.

Noura El-Khoury: :thumbsup: Will do.

--- next day ---

Talia Benson: Draft embargo email snippet:
"Sharing the attached co-marketing kit under embargo until Thu, Mar 14, 2024 09:00 PT. By replying ‘AGREE’, you confirm Northshore Cloud will not publish any related content before the embargo lifts and will use the provided copy and graphics verbatim. Any modifications require written re-approval from Redwood Inference."

Michael Grant: That’s good. Add: “Do not forward outside your launch/review team.”

Soojin Lee: Also specify timezone clearly (PT) + include UTC to avoid confusion.

Tyler Benson: + add the UTM requirement: “Please use these tracking URLs so we can jointly measure performance.”

Ben Carter: Noura, once kit is ready, can you drop link here for final eyeballs?

Noura El-Khoury: Here’s kit v1 (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED (contains doc + 1 slide). Still missing final landing page URL from Elliot.

Elliot Price: Landing page path confirmed: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar
PDF will be linked there; direct PDF URL may change.

Camila Reyes: Skimmed kit. Looks close. Two edits:
1) In the short blurb, remove “industry-leading”
2) Add one sentence: “Benchmarks are directional and depend on workload characteristics.”

Soojin Lee: Also in the marketplace listing copy: replace “lowest cost” with “cost-efficient configurations” (less absolute).

Michael Grant: Please ensure the co-branded slide includes trademark line: “Redwood Inference is a trademark of Redwood Inference, Inc.” and partner logo usage follows their brand guidelines.

Noura El-Khoury: Making edits now. Will re-share v2 in ~1h.

--- later ---

Noura El-Khoury: Kit v2 updated w/ requested edits + embargo boilerplate in the doc footer. Same link.

Ben Carter: Looks good on my end.

Camila Reyes: Approved. Noura you can send to partner once Michael signs off.

Michael Grant: Approved v2.

Tyler Benson: Sending UTM table to Noura via DM now.

Noura El-Khoury: Great. I’ll send to Northshore Cloud today with embargo acceptance request and ask them to confirm their marketplace submission SLA + planned publish time. Will report back here.

Elliot Price: When they schedule publish time, ask them to include the landing page canonical URL (no weird redirects). SEO prefs.

Noura El-Khoury: Will do.
